lines.text: Press a note fifty-seven octaves below middle C.
Imagine counting down from middle C: one octave, two, three, and keep going all the way to fifty-seven.
Scientists translate the pitch of that sound into a note: B flat.
That is a frequency over a million billion times deeper than the limits of human hearing.
lines.cue: caption: A MILLION BILLION TIMES TOO DEEP

lines.text: A sound like that is far too deep for any ear.
lines.cue: caption: TOO DEEP FOR ANY EAR

lines.text: Astronomers found it in a deep observation by NASA's Chandra X-ray telescope.
It's a real sound wave: ripples in hot gas, in a cluster two hundred and fifty million light years away.
And that note has stayed roughly constant for about two and a half billion years.
lines.cue: caption: ROUGHLY STEADY FOR 2.5 BILLION YEARS

lines.text: So what is making a note that deep? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
